meta.title: "You're normal, right?" — why your child feels they have to prove it | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child to recognise pressure through belonging and stay true to themselves. Game-based critical thinking for kids 8–12.

hero.headline: "You're normal, right?" — and your child already agrees
hero.subheadline: One phrase — and they're already proving their "normality" through action. This isn't about character — it's manipulation they don't even notice.

media.alt: A child trying to fit into a group and not look strange

pain.title: "Normal / not normal" is a label, not a question
pain.body:
In class, in a group, in a chat — someone throws out "you're normal, right?" and your child already doubts themselves. They're not sure, but they choose to agree — to avoid looking weird, to avoid falling out of the group.

This isn't about friendship or "normality". It's manipulation through fear of rejection. The child is handed a label and pressured to prove their "normality" through action. Without the skill to recognise this, they agree automatically.

The result — decisions are made not for themselves, but to avoid discomfort. The child gradually loses their sense of self and lives in a constant state of adjusting to others.

solution.title: "Sila Slova" — a detective drama that teaches critical thinking
solution.body: 50 episodes, 13 critical thinking lessons. Your child plays — but is actually learning to protect themselves.
bullets: 🔍 Recognises the "normal/not normal" label as a manipulation tactic
🧠 Understands that "normality" is not a reason to agree

social_proof.quote: My daughter now hears "you're normal, right?" and replies: "yes, that's why I don't do things I don't want to do". I'm so proud of her.
social_proof.author: Elena, mum of 10-year-old Sonya

faq.q: Is this a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at once. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
